title: Apple human interface guidance
summary: Operational Apple HIG rules for platform familiarity, clarity, feedback, and system accessibility settings. Each rule links the HIG page for that subject.

rules.title: Respect platform interaction conventions
rules.intent: Feel at home on the Apple platform in use by reusing patterns people already know and giving that platform its own care
principles: Build on concepts people already know from the platform and the physical world, and keep a behavior consistent once it is established
Design each platform on purpose. An iPhone layout is not a shrunk macOS window
Support the input methods that platform actually offers, including touch, keyboard, and pointer, instead of one desktop control dropped onto a touch screen
antiPatterns: Porting desktop-only controls directly to touch
A custom gesture that contradicts the platform gesture for the same action
acceptance: Navigation, gestures, and controls match the HIG page for the target platform
A second input method still reaches the primary action
limitations: Design principles state the familiarity and platform rules. Control specs live on the linked platform and inputs pages, which this pack does not restate

rules.title: Clarity and focus
rules.intent: Keep the interface direct: only what the task needs, in an order people can scan
principles: Include what the task needs and let the rest recede. Simplicity here means focus, not an empty screen
Make hierarchy obvious with recognizable controls and a stable structure, so people know where they are and what is next
Keep text concise, and set type and layout so the primary content stays legible
antiPatterns: Delight or decoration that blocks the task
acceptance: The first action is identifiable without color
Labels say the action, not a slogan
limitations: Typography and layout pages hold the metric guidance. This rule does not copy type sizes or grid numbers

rules.title: Feedback on interaction
rules.intent: Tell people what happened, what is happening, and what they can do next, at a volume that matches the event
principles: Match the interruption to the stakes: passive status near the item, an alert only for critical and actionable news
Deliver feedback in more than one channel, such as text plus haptics or sound, so it survives a silenced device or VoiceOver
Confirm a significant completed action, and explain why a command cannot run
On watchOS, do not hold attention with an indeterminate spinner. Tell people they will be notified when the work finishes
antiPatterns: No feedback during an asynchronous operation
An alert for a routine success
Color as the only signal that something changed
acceptance: Tap, gesture, success, failure, and in-progress states are each visible
A destructive surprise warns before data loss. An expected delete does not
limitations: Haptic patterns are specified on Playing haptics. This rule only requires a non-visual channel, not a particular haptic

rules.title: System accessibility settings
rules.intent: Honor the person's text size, contrast, and motion settings instead of shipping one fixed presentation
principles: Support larger text, ideally to at least 200 percent (140 percent on watchOS), through Dynamic Type or an equivalent control
When Reduce Motion is on, reduce automatic, repetitive, zooming, scaling, and peripheral motion
Do not use motion as the only way to communicate. Pair it with haptics, audio, or text
Keep custom type at or above the platform's recommended sizes, and larger still if the weight is thin
antiPatterns: A fixed type size that clips or overlaps at the largest Dynamic Type size
acceptance: The screen is checked at the largest text size the platform asks for
With Reduce Motion on, essential information remains without the decorative animation
limitations: The accessibility page states the text-size and Reduce Motion expectations. Exact type ramps stay on the typography page
